name: Korg Wavestation SR
source: Korg Wavestation developer documentation (c)1992 Korg R&D, by Dan Phillips (WSDevDoc.zip from danphillips.com/wavestation/ws_developer.htm via web.archive.org): 'SR Sysex.txt' (header, message types, all formats, patch/performance/wave-sequence structures, parameter numbers 0-484), 'SR Overview.txt' (internal bank numbers, MIDI bank select map, Bank_Exp, SR-only parameters 407-483), 'Developer FAQ.txt' (checksum, Rate_Tab, mix-slope and LFO-increment formulas, 'patches go to the edit buffer and the current Part', SR patch-write bug), 'SR Names.txt' (factory names). Wavestation SR Reference Guide (korg.com, WS_SRReferenceGuide_E.pdf, scanned): parameter ranges on AMP ENV/AMP MOD/BUS ASN/LFO/MIXENV/MIXENVMOD/PATCH/PITCH/WAVES/WSEQ pages, GLOBAL (Protect Int/Card) p.88-89, MIDI (Basic Channel, Perf Mode, 'Param' SysEx receive/transmit) p.96-97, SYSEX DATA XMIT p.129-130, Appendices 2-3. Cross-checked against Edisyn (github.com/eclab/edisyn, synth/korgwavestation: KorgWavestationPatch/Performance/Abstract.java -- ASCII parameter-change builder, 40 ms pacing, bank-number tables, test-performance workaround, write-bug notes; marked librarianTested). Byte layout validated by decoding real dumps: FACTORY.SYX (RAM1/RAM2 patch banks, 4Ch) and FACTORY3.SYX (EX RAM3 = SR ROM4 patches) from danphillips.com/wavestation/SYSEX (factory.zip, factory3.zip): checksums OK, all 105 names match Korg's SR Names list, wave numbers match the PCM list.

korg.channelNibble: Byte 2 = 3n, n = the SR's MIDI Basic Channel - 1 (MIDI page). SysEx is accepted only if n matches; the unit's dumps carry it (Reference Guide p.96, 129).

formats.singlePatchDumpRequest: F0 42 3n 28 10 <bank 0-11 internal> <patch 0-34> F7 -> single patch dump (40h) of that STORED slot. Example RAM3 patch 5, ch 1: F0 42 30 28 10 04 05 F7.
formats.singlePatchDump: F0 42 3n 28 40 <bank> <patch> <852 nybbles> <checksum> F7 = 861 bytes. On receipt the patch goes to the EDIT BUFFER (not memory) and the current Part of the current Performance is switched to play it (Developer FAQ). Answered by 23h (Data Load Complete) or 24h (Data Load Error = bad checksum).
formats.allPatchDump: F0 42 3n 28 4C <bank> <35 x 852 nybbles = 29820> <checksum> F7 = 29828 bytes (~9.5 s at 31250 baud). Patch i = unpacked bytes i*426..i*426+425. Received straight into that bank's memory (needs Protect Int OFF for RAM, Protect Card OFF for a RAM card); answered by 23h/24h. Worked example (FACTORY.SYX, RAM1, ch 1): F0 42 30 28 4C 00 07 05 01 06 06 07 05 06 00 02 04 04 ... 4C F7 -> 07 05 = 57h 'W', 01 06 = 61h 'a', 06 07 'v', 05 06 'e', 00 02 ' ', 04 04 'D' = patch 0 'Wave Dance'; checksum byte 4Ch = (sum of the 29820 nybbles) & 7F. Patch 17 starts at nybble 17*852: 04 04 05 06 02 06 05 07 03 07 03 07 09 07 00 02 06 05 03 05 = 'Debussy VS' (decoded: structure 2 = 4 osc, wave A 161 Sine / ROM11, mix AC -126 +11 +78 +8 -79, BD +4 -88 -4 +87 +4, times 60 60 60 74).
formats.patchWrite: F0 42 3n 28 11 <bank> <patch> F7 -- edit buffer -> memory. BROKEN on the SR: it waits for a front-panel YES that SysEx cannot give (Korg Developer FAQ). Do not use.
formats.parameterChange: F0 42 3n 28 <41|42|43> <num & 7F> <num >> 7> <value as ASCII, max 16 chars, 20h sent as 7Fh> 00 F7. Type 41h for parameter numbers 0-379, 42h for 380-406, 43h for 407+. Value text = decimal integer, positive values with a leading '+' (Edisyn; '0' and '-n' plain). Targets the current Part's patch; per-wave parameters act on the wave chosen by CURRENT_WAVE (79) = 0-3 (A-D). Examples (ch 1): select wave A F0 42 30 28 41 4F 00 30 00 F7; wave A cutoff 75 F0 42 30 28 41 5D 00 2B 37 35 00 F7; wave A level 80 (WAVEA_LEVEL 150) F0 42 30 28 41 16 01 2B 38 30 00 F7; wave A slope 1.00 (stored 50, sent x2) F0 42 30 28 41 19 01 2B 31 30 30 00 F7; SR-expanded PERF_MIDI_MODE (427) = 1 F0 42 30 28 43 2B 03 2B 31 00 F7. Received only with MIDI page 'Param' = RECEIVE or RECV&TRANS; with TRANSMIT or RECV&TRANS the SR also sends these for its own panel edits.
formats.deviceInquiry: F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7 -> F0 7E 0n 06 02 42 28 00 02 00 <minor lsb> <minor msb> <major lsb> <major msb> F7 (family 28 00, member 02 00).
formats.statusReplies: 21h Write Complete, 22h Write Error (memory protected), 23h Data Load Completed, 24h Data Load Error (checksum): F0 42 3n 28 <type> F7.

korg.nybbleOrder: Low nybble first: byte b -> [b & 0F, b >> 4] (0000LLLL, 0000HHHH).
korg.checksum: (sum of all nybble bytes after the header AND after the bank/number bytes) & 7F. Header (F0 42 3n 28 type) and bank/patch bytes are excluded. Validated: all three 4Ch banks in FACTORY.SYX / FACTORY3.SYX check.
korg.byteOrder: Multi-byte fields (uword, long) are big-endian; byte/word signed fields are two's complement.
patchMap: 78-85 S1_MixAC, amt, S2_MixAC, amt, S1_MixBD, amt, S2_MixBD, amt (source u8, amount s8)

90 + 84*w (w = 0..3 = A..D): indiv block, see p.offset; +42..+46 = Pitch/Filter/Amp/Pan/Env1 macro numbers (-1 = USER, not modelled), +74/+78 Lfo1_Inc/Lfo2_Inc (32-bit, derived), +82 Patch_Output bits, +83 Wave_Num_Exp
korg.bankNumbersNote: SysEx/parameter bank numbers are the SR's INTERNAL numbers (SR Overview 2.1): RAM1 0, RAM2 1, ROM11 2, CARD 3, RAM3 4, ROM4-ROM10 5-11. The front panel steps in name order.
korg.midiBankSelectNote: PERFORMANCE selection only: CC32 (CC0 ignored) + PC 0-99, two internal banks per MIDI bank (SR Overview 2.2). Needs MIDI RECEIVE 'Bank Change' ON. Patches have no Program Change.

waveBank.fields: Wave_Bank = indiv byte +2 (0-3; 4+ accepted as RAM3); Bank_Exp = patch byte 88: bit w = 1st expansion, bit w+4 = 2nd expansion for wave w (A=0..D=3). Never set both.
waveBank.decode: b1 = (Bank_Exp >> w) & 1, b2 = (Bank_Exp >> (w + 4)) & 1, wb = Wave_Bank: b2 ? [ROM7, ROM8, ROM9, ROM10][wb & 3] : b1 ? (wb >= 4 ? RAM3 : [ROM4, ROM5, RAM3, ROM6][wb]) : [RAM1, RAM2, ROM11, CARD][wb & 3]
waveBank.encodeNote: [Wave_Bank, expansion] -- expansion 0 = clear both bits, 1 = set bit w (clear w+4), 2 = set bit w+4 (clear w). The Overview's table prints 'B=ROM' for bit 1 / Wave_Bank 3 -- a typo for ROM6 (every other row and the data-structure comment say ROM6).

korg.transmits: With MIDI page Param = TRANSMIT or RECV&TRANS the SR sends 41h/42h/43h parameter changes for panel edits; it also sends program change / bank select (performances), and 23h/24h after every received data message.
korg.sharedWith: EX-8000 / DW-8000 (devices/ex8000.json): same F0 42 3n <model> framing and the same 10h/11h/40h/41h/21h/22h codes. See driverNotes 'COMMON'.

pcmWavesNote: Wave numbers 32-517: pcmWaves[n - 32] (Edisyn's list; 32-515 are the SR ROM waves incl. 'VS 35'-'VS 155' and the EX/A-D expansion waves from 365 on, 516-517 = A/D analog inputs). Wave numbers 0-31 are the 32 wave sequences of the chosen wave bank (names: waveSeqNames).
waveSeqNamesNote: Factory wave-sequence names per bank (Korg 'SR Names.txt'). RAM1/RAM3 are factory defaults the user may have overwritten; RAM2 ships blank; CARD unknown.
factoryPatchNamesNote: Korg's factory patch names (35 per bank). ROM4-ROM11 never change, so a driver can answer requestSlotName for ROM banks without a 10 s bank read; RAM1-3 names must be read (1Ch).
modSourcesNote: Patch modulation sources 0-12 (Reference Guide AMP MOD / LFO pages; Edisyn order). 'ENV1' and 'LFO1/2' on the mix-envelope modulators are Wave A's.

params.note: Number_Of_Waves 0/1/2. 2-osc patches use Waves A and C (AC axis only); 1-osc uses A only.

params.name: Mix Point 0 AC
params.note: Stored 0-254, panel AC = value - 127 (-127 = all A, +127 = all C). Real dumps also hold 128 and 255 for 'centre'/edge; points outside the diamond are clipped. Parameter change: MIX_ENV_POINT (193) = 0, then MIX_ENV_X (195) = stored value 0-254.

params.name: Mix Point 0 BD

params.name: Wave A Wave / Wave Sequence
params.note: Wave_Num (big-endian uword) is the TRUE number: 0-31 = wave sequences of the bank in aBank, 32-515 = ROM PCM waves (names in schema.pcmWaves, index n-32), 516/517 = A/D analog inputs (silent on the SR). Wave_Num_Exp (offset +83) must be written as n >= 397 ? n - 396 : 0. Validated on the EX RAM3 factory bank (Piano Low = 401 GrandPiano, exp 5).

params.name: Wave A Wave Bank
params.note: UI order RAM1..ROM11, CARD. Combined field: Wave_Bank (offset +2) + Bank_Exp bits 0/4 (patch byte 88) -- see korg.waveBank. Only selects which bank's wave sequence plays when the wave number is 0-31; for PCM waves ROM (any non-CARD bank) vs CARD PCM. Parameter change value = internal bank number (korg.bankNumbers).

programs.note: The editable program is a PATCH (35 per bank x 12 banks). Performances (50 per bank) only reference patches (up to 8 Parts) plus effects; the sound itself -- waves, vector mix envelope, filter, envelopes, LFOs -- lives in the patch, and patch parameter changes / single-patch dumps both act on 'the current Part's patch'. Program Change / bank select pick performances, not patches: programChange here re-points the current Part (parameters 57/58), see driverNotes 2.

areas.what: everything (system, RAM1/2 perfs+patches+waveseqs, multisets, perf map, scales; RAM3 etc. follow as separate messages)

backup.restore: Global page: Protect Int = OFF. Send the saved 4Ch / 4Dh / 54h dumps unchanged, one at a time, waiting for 23h (Data Load Completed) after each -- a 4Ch bank is ~10 s on the wire. Wave sequences before patches before performances (Developer FAQ: send referenced items first; a performance last). Protect Int back ON.
backup.notInSysex: Card PCM waves. ROM banks are readable but obviously not writable.

setup: Firmware: the SPECIAL screen (down cursor + BANK + EDIT + +1/YES together) shows the software version; it also holds Init-All-RAM -- do not press anything else there. The SR also answers the universal device inquiry.
MIDI page: Basic Channel = the editor channel (SysEx carries it; SysEx on other channels is ignored).
MIDI page: Param = RECV&TRANS (RECEIVE is enough for editing; TRANSMIT adds panel-edit echo). Default is DISABLE -- with DISABLE no parameter change is received (dumps still work).
MIDI page: Perf Mode = POLY (OMNI also works); MIDI RECEIVE page: Bank Change ON, Program Change ON if you want to step performances from the editor.
GLOBAL page: Protect Int = OFF before storing (bank writes into RAM1-3 are refused while protected); Protect Card = OFF for a RAM card. Set them back afterwards.

Audition setup: press PERF and select a performance you can sacrifice (e.g. RAM1 00) whose Part 1 plays alone (EDT PERF: one part, effects as you like). The editor re-points that Part to the patch being edited; do NOT write that performance afterwards unless you mean to. Edisyn builds the same 'test performance' (one part, full volume, no effects) for this.
Stay at the top performance page (PERF lit, not in a deep edit page) while the editor works: patch dumps land in the edit buffer of whatever patch the current Part plays.
Cable both ways: the SR answers requests and acknowledges every received dump with 23h/24h.
Back up RAM1-3 (patches, performances, wave sequences) before the first store: there is no undo, and a bad bank write replaces 35 patches at once.
uncertain: Edit target: patches are edited through 'the current Part' of whatever performance is playing. Nothing in the docs lets SysEx select a Part number explicitly except parameter 56 CURRENT_PART (not used by Edisyn's patch editor). If the current Part is not the one you hear, edits go elsewhere: setup asks for a one-part audition performance.
requestPatch returns the stored slot, not the edit buffer (no edit-buffer request exists). After unsaved parameter changes a 'get' would revert the editor to the stored version.

Parameter-change value text: the Korg doc only says '7 bit ASCII, 16 characters max'. The '+n' / '0' / '-n' format, slope x2, raw 0-254 mix coordinates and internal bank numbers are from Edisyn (marked librarian-tested); not verified on hardware here. In particular whether option-type params (LFO shape, mod sources, mix loop, bend range -1 = GLOBAL) take the index as text is Edisyn's assumption.

Mix point coordinates: stored 0-254 with 127 = centre per Edisyn; factory dumps also contain 128 and 255. The FAQ's vector-mix equation (xp = X + Y - 255, yp = Y - X) suggests the stored X/Y may be diamond-rotated relative to the panel's AC/BD, and taken literally puts +BD at wave D, while the Reference Guide's diagram puts +127 BD at B. Display here: AC = X - 127, BD = Y - 127 (Edisyn). Check one factory vector patch against the SR's MIXENV page.

MIDI_MODE (parameter 4) values: Edisyn sends 1 then 0 to 'set Multi then Perf' (Developer FAQ step for reaching the top page) and later 4 = 1 + 427 = 1 'to turn off OMNI'. The Korg docs give no value table for 4 or 427; the sequence is copied, not understood.

Wave_Num_Exp: the Korg doc says it is 'added to Wave_Num'. Real EX RAM3 data (FACTORY3.SYX) stores the full number in Wave_Num and n - 396 in Wave_Num_Exp (Piano Low: 401 + 5; 401 = GrandPiano, which matches its name; 406 would be AirSynth). Edisyn decodes num + exp (would read 406) and encodes num = 396 + exp. This schema follows the real data; the SR presumably reads Wave_Num and ignores or cross-checks exp. Test by loading FACTORY3 patch 0 and checking the WAVES page shows GrandPiano.

Derived fields in factory data: Lfo_Inc matches the FAQ formula for fade = 0 and for most fades, but some entries are 0 with a non-zero amount, Mix_Count is 12 instead of RT[10] = 11 on 318 of 420 segments (all flat envelopes), and Mix slopes match 0xFF0000/count (not 0x1000000/count) on most segments. The SR evidently tolerates/recomputes these; recomputing per the FAQ (Edisyn, tested) is assumed safe.
Pitch mod amounts: Edisyn limits them to 0-99; the Reference Guide says +/-127 and factory data holds -60..+127. Used +/-127.

Patch write (11h) and EXECUTE_WRITE: Korg's FAQ says 11h waits for a YES that never comes; Edisyn says the write can be confirmed on the panel. Bank read-modify-write is used instead -- slow (~20 s round trip) and it rewrites all 35 patches.
4Ch bank dumps received while Protect Int is ON: presumably refused with 22h or 24h -- not documented which; the driver should re-read and compare.
Device inquiry member code 02 00 is from the SR doc's generic table; the A/D may answer the same family code with a different member.
Wave numbers 516/517 (A/D analog inputs) exist in the list and in one EX factory patch; on the SR they are presumably silent.
Card bank: Edisyn treats CARD as writable; left write:false here (needs a RAM card, Protect Card OFF, and its own hardware switch).
LFO shape order TRIANGLE, SQUARE, SAWTOOTH, RAMP, RANDOM is the Reference Guide's listing order; factory data only uses 0, 2, 4 (so 1/3 are not cross-checked).
driverNotes: Korg Wavestation SR (Korg 42h, Wavestation family 28h). COMMON with the EX-8000 (one korgDriver): framing F0 42 3n <schema.korg.modelId> <type> ... F7, n = channel() (= the unit's Basic Channel; replies carry it -- match on F0 42 3x <model>, adopt x); shared codes 10h request, 40h single dump, 41h parameter change, 11h write, 21h write complete, 22h write error. Differences: the WS adds bank+number bytes after 10h/40h/11h, nybble data + checksum, ASCII-valued parameter changes, 23h/24h load acks, and banked patches. (1) DATA: unpack nybbles low-first (b = lo | hi << 4) from byte 7 of a 40h message (byte 6 of a 4Ch) up to, not including, checksum+F7; checksum = sum(nybble bytes) & 7F. A patch is 426 bytes (korg.patchMap). Read a param: u8 = byte; s8 = byte >= 128 ? byte - 256 : byte; 'bits' = (byte >> shift) & mask(width) (LFO shape bits 0-6 / sync bit 7, buses = Patch_Output bits 0-3); 'waveNum' = (byte[o] << 8) | byte[o+1]; 'waveBank' = per korg.waveBank.decode with w = p.wave and Bank_Exp = byte 88, value = index into BANKS order (p.options). Name = bytes 0-14, 7Fh and 00h read as space. ALWAYS edit a mirror of the last 426 bytes read: macros (+42..+46), spare bytes, byte 15 and the derived fields are not params. (2) SELECT (programChange(bi, prog)): there is no MIDI program change for patches. Re-point the current Part with parameter changes, exactly Edisyn's tested sequence, ~40 ms apart: 4 = 1, 4 = 0 (MIDI_MODE multi then perf: forces the top page, per the Developer FAQ), 57 PART_PATCH_BANK = bank.select.bank (internal number), 58 PART_PATCH_NUM = prog, then 4 = 1 and 427 = 1 (Edisyn: the patch change drops the SR into OMNI; 427 PERF_MIDI_MODE 1 = POLY). Wait ~300 ms (Edisyn's minimum) before the next dump or request. Remember (bi, prog) as the edit slot. (3) READ: requestProgram(bi, prog) / adoptSlot = F0 42 3n 28 10 <bank.sysex.bank> <prog> F7, wait up to ~1500 ms for 40h (861 bytes, ~0.3 s on the wire); verify checksum. It returns the STORED patch. requestPatch: the SR has no edit-buffer request -- request the remembered edit slot (2) and treat it as the starting point; if no slot is remembered, throw 'pick a patch first'. requestSlotName: ROM4-11 from schema.factoryPatchNames; RAM/CARD from a cached 1Ch bank read (F0 42 3n 28 1C <bank> F7 -> 4Ch, 29828 bytes, ~10 s: timeout 15000 ms; cache per bank, forgetBank clears) -- slice name bytes i*426..+14. requestBank may expose the same read. (4) SEND (sendPatch): F0 42 3n 28 40 <bank> <prog> <852 nybbles of mirror+values> <checksum> F7 with bank/prog = the edit slot. It lands in the edit buffer and the current Part is switched to it (audible at once). Before packing, set every wave's five macro bytes (+42..+46) to FFh (-1 = USER, as Edisyn does) and recompute the derived fields with korg.rateTab (RT) from the values being sent: Mix_CountN = RT[Mix_RateN] for N = 1..4, Mix_Count1B/2B/3B = RT[Mix_Rate1/2/3]; Mix_XSlopeN = trunc(0x1000000 * (Mix_X[N] - Mix_X[N-1]) / RT[Mix_RateN]) (signed 32-bit, truncate toward zero), same for Y; LfoK_Inc = LfoK_Fade == 0 ? floor(0x7FFFFF * LfoK_Amt / 127) : floor(0x7FFFFF * LfoK_Amt / (RT[LfoK_Fade] * 127)); Wave_Num_Exp = Wave_Num >= 397 ? Wave_Num - 396 : 0. (The Developer FAQ's printed code has typos -- comma instead of '=' and wrong Y comparisons; the formula above is Edisyn's corrected version and matches the factory data for LfoK_Inc. Factory dumps show stale counts/slopes in places, see uncertain.) Then wait for F0 42 3n 28 23 F7 (Data Load Completed; ~1500 ms timeout) -- 24h = checksum error: throw. (5) EDIT (sendParam(p, v)): param change on p.pc. Message type by number: < 380 -> 41h, 380-406 -> 42h, >= 407 -> 43h. Bytes: F0 42 3n 28 <type> <pc & 7F> <pc >> 7> <ASCII text> 00 F7, text = (x > 0 ? '+' : '') + x where x = v for plain params, v * p.pcScale for slope (x2), korg.bankNumbers[BANKS[v]] for '*Bank' (waveBank), v for mix X/Y (raw 0-254), and for name params the whole 15-char name (each char; space -> 7F). Prefixes: p.pcWave -> first send CURRENT_WAVE 79 = p.wave (0-3) unless it is already the last one sent; p.pcPoint != null -> first send MIX_ENV_POINT 193 = p.pcPoint unless already selected. Direct per-wave params (WAVEx_* 147-174, buses 362-377) need no prefix. After a structure change (77) the wave/point selection is unknown: resend prefixes. Space messages >= 40 ms (gapMs; Edisyn: 'without this we drop packets'); coalesce to the newest value per param. Mix time/point and LFO amount/fade edits make the mirror's derived bytes stale (the SR keeps its own copy right): recompute them before any later dump (4). Parameter changes are received only with MIDI page Param = RECEIVE or RECV&TRANS and are never acknowledged; the edit buffer cannot be read back, so this can only be checked by ear (setup). (6) STORE (writeProgram(bi, prog, values), RAM1-3 only): the 11h Patch Write is broken on the SR (waits for a panel YES; Developer FAQ, Edisyn). Use bank read-modify-write: 1Ch read of the bank (4Ch reply, ~10 s), replace slot prog with mirror+values (derived fields recomputed as in 4, macros FF), send the whole 4Ch bank with that bank number and a fresh checksum (sum of all 29820 nybbles & 7F), wait for 23h (timeout ~15000 ms; 24h = checksum error; no ack and unchanged data = Protect Int ON), then re-request the single patch (10h) and sameProgram-check. Return the 426 bytes written. Afterwards re-send the edited patch as 40h (4) so the edit buffer and memory agree. (Alternative not used: EXECUTE_WRITE 466 = 1 'works if the object on screen is the one to save' per the FAQ -- too page-dependent.) (7) PROBE: F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7, wait 500 ms for F0 7E 0x 06 02 42 28 00 ...; take the channel from byte 2. Fallback: 10h request of RAM1 00 and wait for 40h. (8) sameProgram(a, b): compare all modelled params decoded from the two images (not raw bytes -- derived fields, macros, 7F-vs-20 name padding and Mix 255-vs-254 differ harmlessly). (9) decode(ev): with Param = TRANSMIT/RECV&TRANS the SR sends 41h/42h/43h for panel edits: parse number = b5 | b6 << 7 and the ASCII text up to 00 (7F -> space; parseInt for numbers). Track 79 (CURRENT_WAVE) and 193 (MIX_ENV_POINT) messages as context; map number (+ wave/point context) to the param with that pc, invert pcScale/bankNumbers, write the mirror, return [{param, value}]. Ignore numbers you don't model (performance, FX, global). Also accept an unsolicited 40h (panel SysEx transmit of a patch) as a full update. 23h/24h/21h/22h are acks -- consume. (10) PACING: >= 40 ms between short messages; >= 300 ms after a patch re-point (2) or a 40h dump before the next request; never start a request while a 4Ch transfer is running. Running status is used by the SR on channel messages only.
